question.text: A non-zero current passes through the galvanometer $G$ shown in the circuit when the key $K$ is closed and its value does not change when the key is opened. Then, which of the following statement(s) is/are true?

options.text: The current through the galvanometer is $40 \mathrm{mA}$.
After the key is closed, the current through the $200 \Omega$ resistor is same as the current through the $300 \Omega$ resistor.

solution.text: $\therefore I_{C}=\frac{10}{100+G}$ $300 I_{3}=\frac{10}{100+G} G$ $I_{3}=\frac{G}{30}\left[\frac{1}{100+G}\right]$ $\therefore \quad I_{3}+I_{G}=\frac{1}{(100+G)}\left[10+\frac{G}{30}\right]=\frac{(300+G)}{(100+G) \times 30}$ According to the problem, $10=\left(\frac{200}{3}+\frac{300 G}{300+G}\right)\left[\frac{(300+G)}{(100+6) 30}\right]$ $Y=R C$ $10=\frac{60000+1100 G}{3} \times \frac{1}{100+G} \times \frac{1}{30}$ $\Rightarrow 900(100+G)=60000+1100 G$ $\Rightarrow \quad 30000=200 G$ $\therefore$ $G=150 \Omega$ $I_{G}=\frac{10}{100+150}=\frac{10}{250}=40 \mathrm{mA}$ As $\quad \frac{200}{100}=\frac{300}{150}$ So, $\quad I_{200}=I_{300}$
